Q937.L1t: Morphine is an opioid analgesic derived from the opium poppy and used for moderate to severe pain.
Q937.L2t: Morphine acts mainly on mu-opioid receptors in the brain and spinal cord to reduce the perception of pain.
Q937.L3t: Opioid receptor activation in the central nervous system depresses neuronal activity, so morphine's central effects include drowsiness and a lowered level of consciousness rather than stimulation.
Q937.L4t: Morphine relieves pain but also produces sedation as a side effect.
Q937.L2f: Morphine is a synthetic compound first made in the 1990s and works by blocking prostaglandin synthesis in peripheral tissues.
Q937.L3f: Morphine acts as a central nervous system stimulant, so its pain relief comes with heightened wakefulness and arousal.
Q937.L4f: Morphine reduces pain and also increases alertness, so it is the stimulating analgesic.

Q922.L1t: Muscle contraction during exercise is powered by ATP, which is regenerated by several energy systems.
Q922.L2t: In high intensity exercise, ATP is used at a very high rate and is resynthesised by phosphocreatine breakdown and anaerobic glycolysis.
Q922.L3t: During intense exercise ADP and inorganic phosphate accumulate while ATP concentration is maintained, and the rate at which the cell can resupply ATP lags behind the rate at which contraction consumes it.
Q922.L4t: Fatigue in high intensity exercise arises when ATP resupply cannot keep pace with ATP demand.
Q922.L2f: Muscle cells hold large ATP stores that last for several minutes of maximal exercise before any other energy system is needed.
Q922.L3f: During high intensity exercise, ADP in the muscle cell is rapidly used up and its concentration drops, which stops ATP from being produced.
Q922.L4f: Fatigue in high intensity exercise is caused by a fall in the cell's ADP concentration.

Q907.L1t: In criminal law, the prosecution must prove every element of the charged offence beyond a reasonable doubt.
Q907.L2t: Intent is a mental state that is rarely proved directly and is usually shown through circumstantial evidence of what the defendant did.
Q907.L3t: A jury instruction that merely allows the jury to infer a fact from proven facts, without requiring it to do so and without shifting any burden to the defendant, leaves the prosecution's burden intact.
Q907.L4t: The instruction was proper because it only permitted the jury to infer intent, which the jury remained free to accept or reject.
Q907.L2f: Arson at common law required the burning of another person's dwelling, and intent was never an element that had to be proved.
Q907.L3f: The instruction told the jury it must find intent once it found that four matches were missing, which relieves the prosecution of proving that element.
Q907.L4f: The instruction was improper because the prosecution must prove every element of the crime beyond a reasonable doubt, and the instruction undermined that.
